The evidence clusters into opposing viewpoints: d1, d3, d4, d8, and d10 report research claiming humans could live up to or beyond 150 years, while d2, d5, d6, d7, and d9 present findings or expert opinions suggesting a maximum limit around 115-122 years or that exceeding 150 is improbable.

The retrieved documents provide directly conflicting answers to the query. Some studies and sources claim a human lifespan limit of 150 years or suggest it is possible [d1, d3, d4, d8, d10], while other research and experts argue there is a lower maximum limit around 115-122 years or that living past 150 is biologically improbable [d2, d5, d6, d7, d9]. Scientific research presents conflicting conclusions on whether humans can live over 150 years. Some studies, often based on analyses of physiological resilience, claim the maximum human lifespan could reach 150 years [d1, d3, d8] or that we are not yet approaching a limit [d4], with some researchers even suggesting future medical advances could enable lifespans of 200 years [d10]. Conversely, other research and experts point to a observed ceiling in maximum age at around 115-122 years [d2, d6, d9], with studies on biological aging concluding the body loses all resilience before 150, making it improbable [d5, d7]. The current verified record remains 122 years [d1, d6, d9].
